In [[mathematics]], and more specifically in [[abstract algebra]], a '''pseudo-ring''' is one of the following variants of a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]]:

* A [[rng (algebra)|rng]], i.e., a structure satisfying all the [[axiom]]s of a ring except for the existence of a [[multiplicative identity]].<ref>{{Cite book
 | last1=Bourbaki
 | first1=N.
 | author1-link=Nicolas Bourbaki
 | title=Algebra I, Chapters 1-3
 | publisher=Springer
 | year=1998
 | page=98
}}</ref>
* A set ''R'' with two [[binary operation]]s + and ⋅ such that {{nowrap|(''R'', +)}} is an [[abelian group]] with [[additive identity|identity]] 0, and {{nowrap|1=''a''(''b''&thinsp;+&thinsp;''c'') + ''a''0 = ''ab'' + ''ac''}} and {{nowrap|1=(''b''&thinsp;+&thinsp;''c'')''a'' + 0''a'' = ''ba'' + ''ca''}} for all ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' in ''R''.<ref name=Natarajan>{{cite journal|last=Natarajan|first=N. S.|title=Rings with generalised distributive laws|journal=J. Indian. Math. Soc. |series=New Series|year=1964|volume=28|pages=1–6}}</ref>
* An abelian group {{nowrap|(''A'', +)}} equipped with a [[subgroup]] ''B'' and a multiplication {{nowrap|''B'' × ''A'' → ''A''}} making ''B'' a ring and ''A'' a ''B''-[[module (mathematics)|module]].<ref name=Patterson>{{cite journal|last=Patterson|first=Edward M.|title=The Jacobson radical of a pseudo-ring|journal=Math. Z.|year=1965|volume=89|issue=4|pages=348–364|doi=10.1007/bf01112167|s2cid=120796340}}</ref>

None of these definitions are equivalent, so it is best{{editorializing|date=July 2024}} to avoid the term "pseudo-ring" or to clarify which meaning is intended.

== See also ==
* [[Semiring]] – an algebraic structure similar to a ring, but without the requirement that each element must have an additive inverse
